summary: Extracted 54 book-wide event cards (ev0001-ev0054) covering all 12 chapters of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, each with time_hint/location/characters/cause/process/result plus caused_by/leads_to causal links, importance rating, and a chNNN#pMM-pNN source citation. Read every chapter shard's full paragraph text directly (not just scene summaries) to ground each event in the actual prose. Event granularity is roughly one event per causal beat, generally 1-2 events per structured_story scene, merged where a scene was pure connective tissue and split where a single scene contained multiple distinct causal beats (e.g. the 102-paragraph Mad Tea-Party scene became 3 events; the 71-paragraph trial scene in ch012 became 5 events).

realistic_adaptation_flags_summary: dream frame (whole narrative retroactively framed as a dream at the end)
talking, anthropomorphic animals and living-card figures (nearly every non-Alice character)
physical size changes (Alice's body repeatedly grows/shrinks by extreme factors)
objects transforming into other objects/beings (pebbles into cakes, baby into pig)
impossible/dreamlike geography (bottomless well, hidden garden reachable only at doll-size, a hall that vanishes)
notes: Per SOUL.md scope, no realistic reinterpretation decisions were made in this task; the events describe the source text faithfully as written, with adaptation-relevant points collected separately in events.json's top-level realistic_adaptation_flags array for Phase 2 (02-worldbuilding/magic-cultivation + world) and H1 user sign-off per bible/WRITE_RULES.md section 7.1.

Character and location names use the source's own wording per scene (e.g. 'King'/'Queen' in ch008-ch009 vs. 'King of Hearts'/'Queen of Hearts' in ch011-ch012, matching structured_story's own present[] field usage); canonical character-ID merge is out of scope here and belongs to Phase 3 character-manager.
Importance grading (major/minor/background) reflects plot weight only; main-line vs. sub-line ownership is story-structure's call, not made here.
